correctness.rationale: For every complex-linear torsion, evaluation on f−f(x)1 vanishes at x, so U is exactly multiplication by the continuous unimodular function u=U1; translation is an invertible isometry, giving the claimed sup norm defect. Lift u to a phase k·x+h(x) on the universal cover, with unique integer k and continuous periodic h. The chordal/geodesic Lipschitz normalization gives ‖k‖₂≤Lip(u): along a lifted straight segment, subdivision into arbitrarily short increments bounds the angular variation by Lip(u) times the length because the angle-to-chord ratio tends to 1; take long segments in direction k and use boundedness of h. The character realizes equality by its directional derivative. In a fixed class, the continuous increment h(x+β)−h(x) integrates to 0, so it vanishes somewhere and the defect is at least the corresponding character defect. This already proves the exact finite minimum, including L=0 and defect 2. For an optimizer with defect less than 2, the phase errors lie, by connectedness, in one closed arc lifted to a real interval of half-width less than π; the mean phase error is at one endpoint (or the interval is a singleton). Continuity and full Haar support force the error to be constant, hence h is invariant and constant in the dense-orbit case. In dimension one irrationality excludes e^(ikβ)=−1 even for continuous non-Lipschitz multipliers, while density yields convergence of the finite minima to zero. The checker was inspected but not executed; grids do not prove these universal bounds or rigidity.
